key_insight: CORTEX adds structured, stage-by-stage reasoning traces to 3D chest CT multimodal models so their answers are more interpretable and traceable to scan evidence.
clinical_relevance: This could improve trust and verification for chest CT AI by aligning model reasoning with radiologist workflow and clinical context.
method: Built a benchmark for 3D chest CT called CORTEX using four reasoning stages: task understanding, visual observation, diagnostic reasoning, and answer synthesis.
Generated reasoning traces with frontier LLMs and then filtered them using automated rubric scoring plus expert radiologist review.
Added stage-level evaluation rubrics co-designed with clinicians for open-ended VQA, closed-ended VQA, and report generation.
evidence_signal: The benchmark is built on CT-RATE and includes 76,177 validated reasoning traces with both structured supervision and stage-level evaluation.
watch_item: As with any LLM-generated supervision, performance may depend on the quality of synthetic traces and on how well the benchmark transfers to real-world clinical settings.
paper_title: CORTEX: A Structured Reasoning Benchmark for Trustworthy 3D Chest CT MLLMs
